Subject: Post-demo econ snapshot — batching & cache test plan

Tom — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and the pragmatic next steps we discussed on the call: 

Summary notes (short):
- Demo covered latency at 99th perc, token unit costs, and fallback routing.
- DataForge is most sensitive to per-1M token economics + predictable peaks for seasonal campaigns.
- Procurement is asking for a 12-month cost estimate and SOC2 evidence.

Competitive positioning (brief):
- Hyperscaler managed endpoints: predictable for standard workloads but unit costs are ~2–3x for small bursty requests after networking + orchestration costs; limited batching for single-tenant burst windows without reserved infra.
- Self-hosted on hyperscaler infra: good raw cost with ops overhead; difficult to guarantee latency SLOs without dedicated pools.
- Redwood: unified runtime with continuous batching, KV/prefix cache and model routing — gives lower median cost for chat-style workloads and supports canary rollouts and fallback variants.

Proposed acceptance tests we discussed (we can run these in a 48–72 hour test window):
1) Per-1M token economics: run three variants for 48h each — hosted (Redwood API), dedicated pool (Redwood Dedicated with small reserved commit), and baseline hyperscaler managed endpoint (your existing vendor) to capture end-to-end unit cost.
2) Batching sensitivity: simulate your traffic and measure cost/latency at batch sizes 1 / 4 / 16.
3) Cache hit-rate sweep: run the same prompt set with 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% artificial prefix reuse to model cache lift.
4) Latency SLO validation: measure p50/p95/p99 and tail variance under peak concurrency burst (10x baseline).

What I need from you to kick off: 
- Sample traffic file (1–2k requests) or a short replay harness we can run in our test harness.
- Preferred window (we can run tests next week; suggested: Tue–Thu).
- Any procurement constraints (do you need a PO/quote first).

Attachments: redwood-econ-snapshot.xlsx (spreadsheet), benchmark-proposal.pdf (test plan).

Thanks — I can put concrete per-1M token numbers in a follow-up once we agree on the test scope.

—
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0126

Michael — helpful recap, thanks. A few quick clarifying Qs before we schedule tests: 

1) Can you send a worked example showing the per-1M token calc (hosted vs dedicated)? Our CFO wants a blended monthly projection for 12 months including average and peak.
2) For batching, our traffic is chatty (avg tokens per turn ~ 120) and we do bursts up to 8k concurrent requests during campaigns — will your test harness simulate that distribution?
3) Procurement (Priya copied) needs SOC2 report and a sketch of data retention/audit logs we will get during the pilot.

We can provide a small sample replay (1,500 requests) but need the test window to be Tue 23 Feb or Thu 25 Feb. Also we may request a short pilot discount depending on results — what's your commercial handle?

On procurement: Priya — can you confirm PO cycles and any vendor security forms we need to expect?

Thanks,
Tom
Principal Product Manager, DataForge
triley@dataforge.com | +1 (206) 555-9842

Tom — answered inline below and attached a simple worked calc for the per-1M token scenario.

1) Worked example (summary):
- Hosted (Redwood API): list price = $0.80 per 1k prompt tokens + $0.20 per 1k completion tokens -> blended example for a 120-token avg turn yields ~ $X.XX per 1M tokens after amortizing streaming overhead and network egress. See attachment 1m-token-calcs.csv for line items.
- Dedicated (reserved pool): unit price drops ~40–60% vs hosted depending on commit and model quantization; for your expected concurrency committed pools tend to reduce tail queuing and costs at scale.
- Hyperscaler managed: your current vendor gave an example earlier (we modeled it at roughly ~1.8x hosted price once orchestration + cross-AZ egress were included).

2) Yes — our harness supports replay with your token distribution and injected campaign bursts (configurable). We'll run the 8k concurrency spike profile.

3) SOC2: we will share our latest SOC2 Type II evidence (vendor evidence packet) and a redacted audit summary; I will loop Security for any extra questionnaire items.

Commercials/pilot discount: for first-time pilots we typically offer a one-time pilot credit or a short-term discount tied to a committed evaluation (details vary by ARR potential). For DataForge I'll propose a 20% pilot credit off hosted units for the test window; Marissa/Finance to confirm.

Proposed schedule: Tue 23 Feb (UTC windows available 14:00–18:00) — please confirm.

Attachments: 1m-token-calcs.csv (CSV with example calc).

Next: once you confirm the sample and window I'll provision a sandbox endpoint and a dedicated monitoring dashboard for the test.

—
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
